comparison: Perfect agreement on testis-specific expression of Tmc7 (C4, C48-C54). Both evaluations find the expression data convincing using multiple independent methods. OpenEval emphasizes convergence across methods and species; peer reviewers accept findings without challenge.

Strong agreement on knockout phenotype characterization (C55-C57, C60-C62). OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive metabolic and fertility testing; peer reviewers accept these control findings establishing specificity of spermiogenesis defects. Peer R16 also includes developmental timing claims (C63, C75) not in OpenEval R2.

Both address infertility phenotype with overlapping claim C60. OpenEval R2 focuses on comprehensive knockout characterization; peer R2 emphasizes the clear infertility phenotype and overall significance of the discovery. Peer R2 includes broader claims (C5, C116, C138) about the main findings.

Strong agreement on spermiogenesis defects (C6-C9, C63-C75). Both find extensive morphological and functional characterization convincing. OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary methods and temporal analysis; peer reviewers confirm phenotypic characterization is well-supported. High Jaccard index (0.833) reflects substantial claim overlap.

Strong agreement on acrosome defects (C76-C81). Both evaluations find PNA staining and TEM evidence convincing for early-onset and persistent acrosome abnormalities. OpenEval emphasizes temporal progression from Golgi phase; peer reviewers confirm findings are highly reliable and convincing.

Both address Golgi morphological defects (C11, C82-C84). OpenEval R5 includes broader evidence with stress markers (C85-C86) and notes causal relationships are inferred; peer R6 accepts Golgi morphology defects and structural characterization without challenge. Peer R6 also includes C126 not in OpenEval R5.

Both address Golgi stress markers (C85-C86). OpenEval R5 includes these as supporting evidence for Golgi dysfunction within broader analysis; peer R11 specifically accepts HSP47 and TFE3 as valid Golgi stress indicators without challenge.

Strong agreement on impaired vesicle fusion (C12, C89). Both find colocalization analysis and TEM evidence convincing. OpenEval notes mechanism remains unclear; peer reviewers accept the interpretation of vesicle trafficking and fusion defects as part of phenotype characterization. Peer R7 includes C136 not in OpenEval R6.

Strong agreement on cis-Golgi localization (C10, C90-C96). Both find multiple approaches convincing including immunostaining colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation. OpenEval emphasizes antibody validation in knockout; peer reviewers state localization results are highly reliable. High Jaccard index (0.727) reflects substantial overlap.

Perfect agreement on reduced cis-Golgi structural proteins (C97-C99, C124). Both evaluations find immunofluorescence and Western blotting data convincing across multiple time points. OpenEval notes mechanism of reduction unclear; peer R4 explicitly states immunohistochemistry clearly indicated reduced GM130, P115, and GRASP65.

Strong agreement on disrupted ion homeostasis (C13, C103-C104, C127). Both find flow cytometry measurements at multiple developmental stages convincing. OpenEval notes direct mechanism not established; peer reviewers confirm revised assays using isolated germ cells adequately address previous concerns. High Jaccard index (0.8).

Perfect agreement on increased ROS levels (C14, C105). Both evaluations find flow cytometry data at multiple time points convincing and statistically significant. Peer R4 explicitly confirms revised assays consolidated this finding in male germ cells.

Both address ROS-stress causation (C15) but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting causal relationships are inferred without experimental validation through interventions; peer reviewers accept Golgi stress observation without challenging the causal interpretation. Low Jaccard index (0.143) reflects minimal overlap.

Both address ER stress (C16, C106-C107). OpenEval R11 rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing correlation vs. causation and lack of temporal validation; peer R12 accepts ER stress markers as part of phenotype without challenge. Moderate Jaccard index (0.6) reflects partial overlap.

Strong agreement on age-dependent apoptosis (C108-C111). Both find TUNEL and Western blotting data convincing with temporal progression suggesting apoptosis is consequence rather than cause. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across markers; peer reviewers accept findings without challenge. High Jaccard index (0.8).

Agreement on overall mechanistic model (C17, C135). OpenEval R13 rates SUPPORTED but notes causal links largely inferred from correlation; peer R14 accepts as reasonable mechanistic interpretation presented as working model. Both acknowledge this synthesizes findings into pathway rather than proving each causal step.

Perfect agreement on ion channel speculation (C121-C122). Both rate UNCERTAIN/speculative. OpenEval notes no direct functional assays presented; peer reviewers explicitly state ion channel function remains to be determined and authors are appropriately careful in presenting this as hypothesis requiring validation.

OpenEval R15 addresses established literature context (C1-C3, C18-C47, C100-C102, C112-C115, C123, C125, C129-C132, C139-C141) as appropriately cited background knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focus on novel experimental findings rather than literature citations.
